claims.text: AARO states it cannot declassify information independently and must request declassification review from the originating offices, with DOPSR reviewing redactions before public release.
'Information must remain classified when its disclosure could reasonably be expected to cause damage, serious damage, or exceptionally grave damage to national security.'

The paper states that classified UAP imagery protects platform capabilities, locations and collection methods, and that even footage of prosaic objects remains classified when derived from sensitive sources.

AARO's September 2025 declassification information paper states the office cannot declassify information independently and must request declassification review from originating offices, with DOPSR reviewing redactions before public release.

edges.label: Process described as immovable was moved by cabinet direction in weeks
edges.note: The September 2025 paper's 'deliberate and time-intensive' declassification account is contradicted by five tranches and over a hundred sensor videos cleared between May and August 2026.

edges.label: The office's own account of why it cannot declassify
edges.note: AARO states it cannot declassify independently, must request review from originating offices, and is bound by DOPSR - a description falsified within eight months by its own department.
